steps: After restart, check the Sandbox mode sidebar badge to verify the actual environment.
Recheck provider addresses, engine installation and login. Host localhost means something different in the container, and paths may need adjustment.
Before importing or changing directories, disable the sandbox and restart, then use sandbox management. Read backup and replacement details before import.
Disable the sandbox and restart to return to ordinary mode. For errors, open the log directory and inspect progress and failures.
tips: Ordinary and sandbox modes maintain separate configuration. Switching does not synchronize changes back automatically.
Consider compatibility permissions only if an engine's inner sandbox cannot run; the interface explains reduced isolation. Sandbox-data deletion is irreversible: inspect what will be retained first.

title: Common settings and troubleshooting
summary: Understand configuration scope, read status and errors first, then make targeted repairs.

sections.title: Check the desktop version and download updates
steps: On desktop, open Settings → System settings → Desktop updates to inspect the current version.
Click Check for updates to find the latest official GitHub release. If newer, click Download from GitHub.
Choose your system's installer on the release page, finish active work and install it yourself.
tips: Desktop checks once daily without automatically downloading, installing or restarting. Only a newer official Release triggers an update, not code pushes or drafts.
Retry failed checks later. The web version has no desktop-update entry.

screenshot.alt: Current desktop version and update-check entry in system settings
screenshot.caption: Check manually, then download from GitHub when an update is available.

sections.title: Concurrency, assistants and display
steps: When running many tasks, set task and conversation capacity in global Concurrency limits or project configuration, and inspect effective values.
If scheduled tasks should not consume capacity, verify adequate resources before enabling that option. Excess tasks and chats queue.
Configure each assistant's engine and model under Assistants. Check step-execution and task-coordinator settings separately.
Change the user name in system settings. Language, fonts, size and skins are under Settings → Appearance; repository scanning scope is under Git settings.
tips: Changing the default execution engine affects new tasks and steps, not existing task or step settings.

screenshot.alt: Global task and conversation concurrency limits
screenshot.caption: Set global capacities and the scheduled-task exception.

sections.title: Troubleshoot in order
steps: If a task does not start, distinguish ready, queued and waiting-for-review states. Check starting step, automatic startup and engine availability.
On execution failure, read the latest error. Check SDK installation, provider authentication, model name, network and file permissions, then rerun.
For history or API loading errors, use Retry. If the API returned a webpage, confirm backend version and restart using your usual method.
If native session history was lost, read Rerun with a new session, supply current goals and required artifact references, and do not treat it as full native-context recovery.
For missing artifacts or remote access failure, check actual file generation or host availability, address, key and authorization expiry respectively.
tips: When reporting issues, include version, OS, engine, reproduction steps and redacted error screenshots, never credentials. Without an explicit setting, 20 continuous minutes without engine events triggers the idle timeout while retaining the session. Existing custom timeouts remain; 0 disables it. Quiet thinking or tools are not necessarily stalled: inspect logs before rerunning.

screenshot.alt: Demonstration failure caused by a nonexistent model
screenshot.caption: The error says the chosen model is unsupported. Repair the step's model configuration before running again; it is not repaired in this image.

title: Appearance, skins and languages
summary: Choose personal display preferences or create previewable skins and language packs through ordinary project chat.

sections.title: Choose a built-in language
steps: In Settings → Appearance, choose Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, English, Japanese, French, German or Arabic and inspect common entries and date controls.
On the website, use the top language dropdown for Chinese, English, French, German or Arabic. Your browser saves the choice; without a saved preference, browser language is detected.
tips: French, German and Arabic app translations currently cover major entries; other strings may remain Chinese, and the app's Arabic layout is still left-to-right. Website and manual text follow the top language selector, with right-to-left Arabic layout. Real screenshots remain Chinese. Language switching does not translate past conversations or user files.

screenshot.alt: Built-in language selectors in the app and website
screenshot.caption: Real screenshots of the added language choices are pending.

sections.title: Use v2 skin layouts and feature extensions
steps: Under Settings → Appearance, install and validate a trusted v2 skin, preview and apply it. For features such as notes, ask the author in appearance-creation chat to include components.

Read the enablement confirmation for packages with code. Updating a package or changing identity may ask again. Open panels through the skin's menus or feature entries, which depend on the package. Notes or calendars are not preinstalled app features.
The package can position the composer above, below, left or right. Compact views retain vertical arrangement. After switching, check messages, composer and settings remain usable.

Extension data is separate by browser identity, device, skin and feature. Switching or deleting a skin does not erase it. Use the extension's own export for backup. If the interface breaks, add skin=default to the URL and refresh.
tips: Component code has the current page's privileges. Enable trusted sources only. Cancelling preview restores appearance but does not undo code already executed.
Extension data is not included in skin ZIP exports or synchronized between browsers/devices. Back up before clearing storage; failed saving must not be treated as success.

screenshot.alt: v2 component enablement confirmation and feature-panel entry
screenshot.caption: Real execution screenshot of a trusted demonstration package is pending. Format validation is not visual acceptance.

sections.title: Choose and save personal appearance
steps: For full-device access, open Settings → Appearance. Project-authorized users enter Appearance and skins from the sidebar.
Choose font, size and language. Search or filter installed skins, preview then apply. The fixed preview bar lets you cancel or confirm.

Authenticated Gateway users' choices are saved per account and device, restoring in another browser on the same device. Retry failed saves. Local choices without platform login remain in this browser.
tips: Packages and creation records are shared on the device; personal selections are isolated. Project-authorized users can only choose installed packages.
Missing or broken packages fall back to default appearance. Add ?skin=default or ?language=default to restore the default skin or Simplified Chinese.

screenshot.alt: Fonts, size, language and installed skins in Appearance
screenshot.caption: The real settings page shows defaults and built-in examples on the right. No personal preferences were changed.

sections.title: Create skins and languages through chat
steps: With host-management rights, click Let's discuss appearance, choose an installed, verified engine and describe a goal, such as: Make a dark skin, preserve layout and use an upward send arrow.

Chat is on the left, editing and preview on the right; phones switch tabs. Adjust name, colors, font, size, send icon and layout, then Save adjustments into the same draft package. Editing is disabled while chat runs. Check PC and phone previews.

For a language pack, ask in the same chat, for example: Add Spanish while preserving appearance. Switch the right side to Language. It loads after generation; use Read and validate to check its directory, coverage, missing strings and examples.

For skins, click Save appearance and preview; for languages, Install and preview. Confirm or cancel in the preview bar. Saving to the library does not confirm personal application. Export ZIP to reuse, and inspect replacement prompts for same-ID imports or updates.
tips: Creation reuses the fixed Runtime project and ordinary chat, invoking your model. Continue earlier work through Conversation history above the window. Preview examples themselves do not run tasks.

Fonts use installed system fonts. Historical messages and files are not automatically translated. Built-in send icons can be selected in adjustments; custom vector icons must be supplied by a validated draft.

Language packs are independent of skins and currently support left-to-right languages. Missing strings and date controls use the specified built-in fallback. Coverage does not prove translation quality; use chat to update outdated string catalogs.

screenshot.alt: Chat and editing/preview areas in appearance creation
screenshot.caption: An authorized empty creation chat and adjustment form. Its composer is prefilled; no message was sent, model run or skin saved.

sections.title: Read and preview a language pack
steps: Switch the appearance studio's right side to Language and check Language-pack directory. Generate through the same chat or import an existing language ZIP.
Generated packs load automatically. Read and validate checks coverage, missing strings and examples. A waiting-for-generation notice for an empty directory means creation is unfinished.
After validation, Install and preview, then confirm or cancel personal application. Coverage cannot replace a translation-quality review.
tips: Only left-to-right languages are currently supported. Date controls and missing strings use the pack's specified built-in fallback.

screenshot.alt: Language directory and validation entry in an empty creation chat
screenshot.caption: The Language tab offers directory, Read and validate and ZIP import. No language pack has been generated, installed or applied.

title: Project remote-operation audit
summary: Inspect remote visitors' actions and whether they succeeded, were denied or failed.

sections.title: Filter and inspect remote operations
steps: On the device hosting the project, open the local project's Configuration → Operation audit. Remote projects, Gateway workspaces and project-bound access do not offer this tab.
Filter by action and result, then inspect actor, time, source and task, workflow or file identifier.
Go to the next page or first page, refresh for latest records and retry failed loading.
tips: This audit covers remote-source actions and denied/failed results, not full chats, and stores no credentials. The API is local-only on the host. Default retention is 30 days; follow the page's actual duration. Public share visitors' real names are unknown; Remote browser (self-reported identity) is not authenticated identity.

screenshot.alt: Audit filters and empty records for a local project
screenshot.caption: The actual local audit entry and action/result filters. No remote records exist in the demonstration project; no actions or identities were fabricated.

title: Frequently asked questions
summary: Understand engines, model services, file changes and recovery boundaries before starting.

sections.title: How do SDK and CLI differ, and which should I start with?
steps: Both are engine integration methods for model capabilities. SDK integrates through developer APIs; CLI runs command-line programs. Neither is a model name.
Start by installing Codex SDK or Claude Agent SDK, complete authentication, choose and verify a model, then make it the default execution engine. Existing CLI users may choose that engine instead.

The provider supplies service address and authentication, the model identifies what handles the request, and the engine provides sessions, tools and execution. Follow the selected engine's form; credentials are not necessarily interchangeable.
tips: SDK installation only establishes runtime dependencies, not authentication, permissions or quota. Distinguish Codex and Claude Code SDK entries from those marked CLI.

screenshot.alt: SDK and CLI choices in engine settings
screenshot.caption: Inspect recommended SDK engines and their separate installation and verification states.

sections.title: How are software and model calls charged?
steps: Check the selected model service's plan, authentication and quota before a small initial task. An SDK itself is not model credit.
Task execution, automatic review, assistants and retries can all invoke models. Inspect models separately in step, review and assistant settings.
Use execution analysis to inspect usage and cost sources. Estimates help explain consumption; final charges follow the service provider's rules and bill.
tips: Do not assume downloading an SDK or signing in makes calls free, or that one subscription applies to every engine.

screenshot.alt: Token usage and cost sources in execution analysis
screenshot.caption: Provider-reported cost and coverage are shown. Estimated cost is labeled only when pricing estimates are actually used.

sections.title: Where is data stored, and can AI modify my files?
steps: Local tasks, workflows and messages are stored in project .workstep by default. Disabling Data directory follows project directory uses ~/.workstep/projects/<项目ID>/. The project's .workstep/project.json reassociates original data.

Requests and context read by the engine may be sent to your configured model service. Channels, sharing and remote access also disclose information within their authorized scope to the corresponding parties.
AI with write permission can modify project files. Practice in a separate project, check permissions before execution and inspect Git diffs and actual artifacts afterward.
Sandbox associations still modify original mounted files. Task Worktrees provide separate directories, but merge results still need inspection.
tips: Local storage does not mean offline model calls. Keep keys, account credentials and irrelevant sensitive files out of task descriptions, attachments and screenshots.

screenshot.alt: Conversation permission-mode panel on a phone
screenshot.caption: Default, Read-only, Workspace write and other choices are listed. Actual support and behavior depend on the engine.

sections.title: How do stopping, retrying, rework and recovery differ?
steps: Stopping interrupts current execution or a reply but does not undo files already written. Inspect existing results before continuing.
Retrying or rerunning invokes the engine again, possibly continuing context or using a new session as prompted. It does not revert every change to its pre-run state.
Rework corrects outputs according to review feedback or return connections, subject to workflow dependencies and limits. Read confirmations when rerun scope changes.
After reopening WorkStep, inspect task and session state first. Engines supporting recovery may resume their native session; lost native records require a new session and rerun.
tips: Automatic recovery depends on engine and available history. Full recovery is not guaranteed for every engine or interruption.

screenshot.alt: Reset step selected in a completed task
screenshot.caption: This completed task has Reset step selected, affecting only the next step message. It is not a deletion confirmation or missing-session warning.
